title: USF women's lacrosse team prepares for conference tournament with historic goals in sight - Sunshine Sentinel
text:
The University of South Florida women’s lacrosse team is preparing for the American Conference tournament, according to an April 29 announcement. The Bulls, ranked No. 25 and holding a regular-season title, are seeking their first bid to the NCAA Tournament in just their second season.
This development is significant as it marks a rapid rise for a program that only began competition last year. Head coach Mindy McCord challenged her players before the tournament by saying, “At some point in my career, I’ll be here standing in front of some USF team that’s going to accomplish a regular-season championship, a conference tournament championship, and the program’s first bid to the NCAA Tournament. That is going to happen. Who will that team be? Why not you?”
Senior attack Elise Grissett said, “Oh my gosh, we are bound and determined to be that team… We were built the right way. We were built to peak, and we are motivated to get this done.” Freshman goalkeeper Natalie Eastwood added, “We want that team to be us… So you better believe there’s a drive within every single one of us — especially to do it for the people who sacrificed so much and allowed us to have this opportunity.” McCord also said her vision was always about building toward championships: “From the start, we were recruiting players to win championships as soon as we could. But it usually takes more time than this.”
The Bulls finished their inaugural season with a 13–5 record and set an attendance record at Corbett Stadium with over 2,386 fans at their opening game on Feb. 7, 2025 against Kennesaw State. They finished as runner-up in last year’s American Conference Championship after drawing more than 10,000 total fans during the season.
McCord came from Jacksonville University where she led teams for thirteen seasons and accumulated over twenty-one regular-season and conference titles along with eight NCAA Tournament appearances.
Looking ahead at Thursday’s semifinal against Temple—whom they previously defeated—the Bulls hope another victory will secure them both another trophy and entry into NCAA history books.
Tickets can be purchased by calling 1-800-GoBulls or visiting USFBullsTix.com.
